course_description:
Advanced digital filtering: polyphase, multirate, all-pass, lattice and IIR filters. Signal conditioning, analogue filter types, sigma delta converters. Fast algorithms; Cooley-Tukey FFT, mixed radix formulations, Good-Thomas algorithm. Autoregressive, moving average signals. DSP applications and programming.

This course is an introduction to the exciting and rapidly advancing field of digital signal processing. These daysﾠ Digital Signal Processing has largely replaced analog electronics for virtually all applications.ﾠ DSP technology levers off computer hardware that becomes cheaper and faster every year, so a DSP solution will invariably replace analog solutions over time.ﾠ The course will be delivered in a practical manner and students will be asked to code algorithms in Matlab to demonstrate deep and practical understanding of the course material.ﾠDSP research strengths at UQ will be highlighted and applications of DSP in commodity devices such as CD and DVD players will be used as course examples.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

Course was rated highly by students last year so no significant changes were necessary. The exam will be invigilated and identity verified as it will be a traditional paper exam on-campus. Some changes will be made to tutorials to further assist students with their assignments.

AI Statement

This course does not make explicit use of AI tools in its teaching or assessment. Students are expected to complete all work in accordance with standard academic integrity requirements.

course_aims: It is expected that upon successful completion of the course, students will haveﾠdeveloped the ability to code and understand advanced Digital Signal Processing algorithms.ﾠ The ability to code well-known Digital Signal Processing algorithms reinforces a solid understanding of the algorithms and gives the student a solid skill base for their future career.

learning_outcomes.description: Implement Digital Signal Processing algorithms in MATLAB
Use and apply data windowing appropriately to solve a range of filtering and analysis problems
Code fundamental DSP algorithms such as the FFT and multi-rate filters
Be able to describe the DSP processing chain of DSP-based devices such as a CD player
Acquire an international perspective on the field through the advanced topics delivered by guest lecturers and recognized researchers

assessment_details.task_description: This task is designed to assess your understanding of convolution and your ability to apply it effectively across a series of questions. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex.
